paper.title_en: Lightest hidden-strangeness nuclei with HAL QCD-motivated ϕN interactions
paper.abstract_en: •QCD based ϕN interactions generate bound ϕN, ϕNN, ϕNNN, and ϕNNNN systems.•Bound states are predicted for <math altimg="si23.svg"><msubsup><mrow/><mi>ϕ</mi><mn>3</mn></msubsup></math>H, <math altimg="si24.svg"><msubsup><mrow/><mi>ϕ</mi><mn>4</mn></msubsup></math>H, <math altimg="si24.svg"><msubsup><mrow/><mi>ϕ</mi><mn>4</mn></msubsup></math>He, and <math altimg="si25.svg"><msubsup><mrow/><mi>ϕ</mi><mn>5</mn></msubsup></math>He.•The embedded ϕ meson compresses the nuclear core.•Universal correlations relate few-body binding energies to ϕN scattering parameters. We present results for light ϕ-mesic nuclei with <math altimg="si28.svg"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math>–5 obtained in the framework of Faddeev and Faddeev–Yakubovsky equations in configuration space with HAL QCD-constrained ϕN interactions in the ϕN(<sup loc="post">2</sup>S1/2) and ϕN(<sup loc="post">4</sup>S3/2) channels. Binding is driven by the strongly attractive ϕN(<sup loc="post">2</sup>S1/2) channel, leading to bound ϕNN, ϕNNN, and ϕNNNN systems, where the ϕ meson acts as a deeply bound impurity and induces compact nuclear configurations. Interaction in the <sup loc="post">4</sup>S3/2 channel is sufficiently attractive to support bound states in nuclei with mass number A ≥ 4. Inelastic effects, included via a complex potential, have little impact on binding energies while producing moderate widths, indicating possible experimental observability. We find universal correlations between binding energies for <math altimg="si28.svg"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math>–5 and scaling with the ϕN scattering length, demonstrating that these systems are largely governed by two-body physics.
